reason: The sole operative sentence of Executive Order 8341 revokes Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee) and made related changes to customs ports and districts; its operative words are 'is hereby revoked'. A present-tense revocation with no later effective date is carried out when the order takes effect, so the command was exhausted by performance on the order's signing date, 1940-02-08, which is recorded as the end. The filing date February 9, 1940 and the issue date February 10, 1940 are the alternatives if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. The Federal Register docket line reads 'Filed, February 9, 1940;' and the issue is headed 'Washington, Saturday, February 10, 1940'.

Paragraph 1 closes the departments and excuses employees from duty on one stated day: the text says the offices "shall be closed all day on" on "Tuesday, December 24,1940". The command is performed and spent on that day, December 24, 1940.

Paragraph 2 directs that the order "shall be published in the" Federal Register. The held text is the Federal Register issue headed "Washington, Wednesday, December 18, 1940", and the order's filing line reads December 17, 1940; the direction was performed by publication in the December 18, 1940 issue (5 FR 5143) and is spent then.

The order revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, and states when: "This order shall become effective at" "the close of business January 15, 1941". A one-time revocation is performed when it takes effect, so the command is spent at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The end is recorded as 1941-01-15.

The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking November 20, 1954 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on November 20, 1954 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to December 20, 1954 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.
